messages:
marta: Heads up — hosted canary started flapping on long-seq P95 after last night's release (merged PR #4321). CI perf job flagged a ~22% P95 regression on the kvcache workload.

sam: saw this in dashboards too, good catch. which trace do we want to start with?

marta: tagging the CI job: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/infra/perf/kvcache-longseq-1. Root cause suspicion: the kernel auto-selection change + new batching heuristics. Perf-bot attached the failing run.

perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression detected: kvcache-longseq P95 +22% vs baseline 1783400000. Regression started at commit 9f3a2b7 (engine: prefer AMP kernel for Llama-like shapes).

ali: I kicked off a local micro-benchmark reproducer with seq=2048, batch=4. Baseline (before 9f3a2b7): 480ms P95. After merge: 590ms P95. KV cache hit rate looked the same, but token decode time jumped.

jess: did you capture profiler? please paste flame graph or perf counters.

ali: attaching snippet from perf tools:
```
# top hotspots (sample count)
translate_kernel_select()  42%
matmul_kernel_optim()      25%
kv_cache_lookup()          8%
decode_step()              15%
```
Looks like kernel selection overhead increased, but also some unexpected memcpy work for KV cache when using the new batching path.

chris: interesting — the new batching path introduced a copy-on-batch step to normalize kvcache shapes. That was intended to reduce branch mispred but could add memmove cost for longer seqs.

sam: can we bisect quickly? which commit boundaries are suspect?

marta: started git bisect between before-9f3a2b7 and after-merge. Early result points to the kernel selector change + the batching refactor landed in PR #4378 (same window).

jess: given this is a release blocker for canary, recommend revert of kernel selector first (smaller blast radius) while we finish perf analysis. I'll open a revert PR.

marta: +1, please also hold rollout to remaining hosts. Deploy-bot: hold canary rollout: reason=perf-regression, ticket=ENG-1189

deploy-bot: Action: canary rollout paused for release/2026-03-17.

ali: ran revert locally (reapplied old selector), re-ran microbench. P95 back at ~485ms. Good signal.

marta: ok revert merged and rolled back on canary. Now follow-up work: we need reproducible unit tests and tighten thresholds in CI so this doesn't slip again.

sam: proposing changes: 1) add targeted microbench in CI: kvcache-longseq with seq=2048, batch=4, run 3 measurements and compute trimmed mean/P95; 2) set regression threshold to +10% for P95; 3) require deterministic RNG seeding for the bench to reduce flakiness.

jess: also add a perf-bucketed canary job that runs during rollout (lightweight) and fails fast on >10% regression.

ali: fixed flaky test where bench harness used system time for seeding. changed to `--seed=$CI_JOB_ID` so runs are deterministic per job. Also reduced background jitter in the harness.

chris: for kernel selector: we'll add a fast-path decision table for long-seq shapes to avoid copy-on-batch memmove; and land it behind a feature flag for gradual rollout.

marta: captured action items: 
- jess: revert PR merged, follow-up issue to harden selector logic (ENG-1190)
- ali: add deterministic seeding + harness fix (PR queued)
- sam: add microbench job + threshold + alerting (PR queued)
- chris: design fast-path + feature flag (design doc link forthcoming)

jess: retro note: perf CI needs to report signal-to-noise and run 3 independent retries by default for P95 tests. Flaky perf tests hide systematic regressions.

marta: thanks team. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and mark this as resolved for canary, but keeping follow-ups open until selector refactor lands and microbench is in CI. :white_check_mark:

sam: quick Q — do we want to add an automated bisect job for future regressions? could be expensive.

jess: probably as an opt-in for suspect windows. For now let's rely on faster local bisect + perf-bot annotations. Longer term, infra can spin up distributed bisecter.

perf-bot: [info] linked issues: ENG-1189 (canary perf alert), ENG-1190 (selector harden), ENG-1191 (ci-microbench).
